newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks prop Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Banks prop Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market edged barely higher at the opening on Tuesday with the big banks propping up the market on hopes of an interest rate easing.
At the open, the All Ordinaries index added one point to 2,427.9.
Brokers said that with unconvincing signals again from offshore, traders again stayed on the fence as they awaited the results of today's Reserve Bank of Australia board meeting.
"We are looking for a repeat of Monday's performance with only a few points in it either way," said a Sydney broker.
The big banks climbed back towards the top of their recent high ranges before slipping from early highs.
"The banks are doing most of the work even though they are starting to come off now. CommBank is the strongest there, its still playing catchup to the others," the broker said.
Commonwealth Bank shares soared to fresh highs early, touching A$13.20 (US$10.11) before easing back with the rest of the sector.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 47 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
